notes: gateMaxPx2 60 = max(measured x 1.2, measured + 60) over the measured 0 px2 masked non-chart area after r3 (plan §16 #30), 2026-09-26: the family's area fell from 9,656 px2 (browser vs PowerPoint 8,768, ours 8,798 of it by arbitration) to 0. It was the emitter fitting every cover crop a second time on top of the crop the extractor had measured — row 1 frame 4 showed the portrait's middle sixth stretched over its frame (the white line PowerPoint drew), row 2 frame 4 a window from the middle of the source instead of its bottom, the cover frames' edge slivers the same doubled crop. A regression guard, not a target.
Twenty-one images, no shapes and no rasters: rows 1 and 2 twelve, row 3 five frames plus the four tiles of its repeated background (r3; one picture per visible tile, plan §16 #30).

Crops follow Blink's painting: an 's destination rect is snapped to whole pixels before its source rect is mapped, so a 400 x 300 source covering 180 x 140 is painted 186 px wide from -3 (crop 3/186 each side), not 186.67 from -3.33; background tiles keep fractional sizes and positions, and a no-repeat tile starting inside its painting area starts on the snapped pixel. Measured on a coordinate-coded probe (engine/fixtures/fidelity/crop_evidence.py).
Twelve of the images are rows 1 and 2. The frames are 180 x 140 at x = 40/245/450/655/860/1065
and y = 70/300/530, and the sources are 400x300 (4:3 PNG), 300x400 (3:4 JPEG) and 160x160 (RGBA PNG),
so each object-fit mode crops in a different direction and the numbers below are checkable by hand.
The SVG asset stays kind 'image': 02-IR-SCHEMA.md §image says the extractor rasterises it to a PNG
at displayed size and emits a warn diagnostic — it is not a 'raster' element (11-WP1's table says
'isolated raster at displayed size', which means the same rasterisation, not a different kind).
src on every image is an absolute file path once extraction has resolved it through assets_dir.
Before r3: gateMaxPx2 11,588 = max(measured x 1.2, measured + 60) over 9,656 px2 on fidelity-w3 (2314d7f), 2026-09-25 (plan §11; Peter #16); re-set above where the area fell.
